A horizontal line parallel to the x-axis can be added in matplotlib using `plt.axhline()`, which intersects the y-axis at a specified value. To emphasize its relation to the y-axis, the line spans the entire width of the plot horizontally. Here's an example:

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.plot([1, 2, 3, 4], [10, 15, 13, 17], label="Data")  # Sample data
plt.axhline(y=13, color='red', linestyle='--', label='Threshold')  # Horizontal line at y=13
plt.ylabel('Y-axis')
plt.xlabel('X-axis')
plt.legend()
plt.title('Horizontal Line at y=13')
plt.show()
```

This code draws a dashed red horizontal line at `y=13`, highlighting its alignment with the y-axis value, and outputs a plot where the line extends across the entire x-range. The `y` parameter defines where it intersects the y-axis.
